description: Big Dad hooks (one process per event: post_tool.py = context guard + watch + output shrink + background output watch, pre_compact.py = read guard reset + slim compact): read guard (no second copy of an unchanged file while the first is in context; also Bash/PowerShell commands that only dump such a file, BIGDAD_BASH_GUARD=off), context guard (one-line note when a call re-sends more than the per-call cost guide: 130k or ~65% of the real window after setup; also inside subagents), watch (after `bigdad.py watch`, logs big tool outputs for the rest of the session, its subagents' too), slim compact (PreCompact instructions: drop superseded reads, written text, finished agents; the user's own /compact text comes first), agent monitor (SubagentStart/Stop -> agents.jsonl, numbers only), redirect detector (the user ends a plan: 'scrap this', 'start over'; one note per 8 turns in a heavy chat, and the next slim compact drops the old plan; softer phrases like 'never mind' get a note only). Output shrink (a big noisy Bash/PowerShell output from tests, installs, builds, git log/diff, find... is cut after it ran, never the command: errors, warnings, failures and the end kept, full output saved and named; failed calls never cut). Output cap (2.0.5): any other Bash/PowerShell output over 4,000 chars that is not a file read keeps its start and end, full output saved and named in the note where the middle was. Background output watch (2.0.5, bg_watch.py): a background job's output file read whole again after it doubled, and a background job piped into `| tail`, each get one short note. Off switches: BIGDAD_SHRINK, BIGDAD_READ_GUARD, BIGDAD_BASH_GUARD, BIGDAD_GUARD, BIGDAD_WATCH, BIGDAD_LOOP, BIGDAD_SLIM, BIGDAD_AGENTS, BIGDAD_REDIRECT, BIGDAD_BG_WATCH, BIGDAD_AGENT_GUARD (helper notes only), BIGDAD_SIDE (the /btw tip) = off. Main-chat pause: OFF by default (`bigdad.py pause 2`). Loop detector (only after `bigdad.py watch`): the same call 4+ times with no edit in between gets a one-line note. SessionStart: nothing for Claude (bench: that line made Haiku think on plain tasks); for the user the baseline, a version note once per new Claude Code version (no network), and a load record the opt-in sentinel (`bigdad.py sentinel on`, a user-level hook outside this plugin) checks. At every startup and /clear (2.0.6) one background refresh (detached, no window, one at a time): the profile is rebuilt only when the setup fingerprint moved (Claude Code version, skills, plugins, MCP servers, hooks, window settings), without running any hook, and the baseline is updated from new or changed logs only (per-log cache; the full rebuild stays the 7-day fallback); BIGDAD_REFRESH=off keeps the 2.0.5 7-day baseline rebuild only. Learning first (2.0.6): on an install with no usable baseline no hook blocks, cuts or notes anything (opt-ins the user turned on still act); each only counts what it saw, until the baseline covers 30 calls (BIGDAD_LEARN_CALLS) and a profile exists, then one line says it is on; an install that already has a baseline never learns; BIGDAD_LEARN=off acts at once. Windows, a Big Dad file another process holds open (2.0.6): a hook waits 0.2 s on saves only, a bigdad.py command 2.5 s on saves, reads and removes; still held, the old file stays whole. Hard stop for subagents (fallback after autoCompactWindow): OFF by default (`bigdad.py agent-stop 100k` caps each subagent at 100k tokens per call; 1-20 = x the guide; 80% heads-up; past the cap only its handoff under ~/.claude/bigdad/handoffs/, then one relaunch line in the main chat; the gated sh check costs ~13 ms median (max ~23 ms) per tool when off, no Python).
